prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: hit while turning left in Houston, Texas. Injury: knee injury. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1066; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record for this exercise, so you can call me the plaintiff.

Q: Fair enough. Where were you on the day of the accident?
A: I was driving through an intersection in Houston, Texas, heading toward a shopping center on my side of the road.

Q: What were you doing right before the collision?
A: I had my turn signal on and I was turning left. I'd slowed down, looked both ways, and started into the turn when another vehicle came straight through the intersection and hit the front driver's side of my car.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not clearly. I saw headlights, but I didn't have time to react. It happened in a second.

Q: After the impact, what did you notice about your body?
A: My left knee hit the dashboard and the steering column. It hurt immediately, and I could barely bend it. I sat there for a minute before I got out.

Q: Did you seek medical care that day?
A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They took X-rays and told me there was no fracture, but there was swelling and they said I had a serious sprain and possibly ligament damage.

Q: Since then, what treatment have you received for the knee?
A: I've been going to physical therapy about three times a week. I also had an MRI, and I was given a brace and crutches for several weeks. My orthopedic doctor has talked with me about possibly needing further evaluation if the pain doesn't improve.

Q: How has the knee affected your daily life?
A: It's made a lot of things harder. Stairs are difficult, especially going down. I used to walk my dog every morning and now I need help with that. I've had to stop playing recreational softball, and I can't stand for long periods at my job without discomfort.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: Yes, I was out for a stretch right after the accident and then worked reduced hours while I was in therapy. I'm still working, but I'm not doing the same amount of physical tasks I used to.

Q: Do you have any prior injuries to that knee?
A: No, nothing that required treatment. I had normal use of that leg before this happened.
